text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — tail latency spike detected for /v1/generate (model: redwood-large@int8-calib-2026-03-14). p95 jumped to 800ms, p99 to 3.2s, streaming stalls reported. Auto-escalation triggered.

ryan (oncall): Got it. I'm on page. Looking at console now (https://console.redwood/inference/telemetry). Any recent deploys or config changes?

maya (oncall-next): I saw the int8 calibration rollout finished ~15m ago for several canaries. Could be related.

raj (eng-runtime): Confirmed: yesterday at 2026-03-14T02:04Z we pushed int8-calib-2026-03-14 profile to canary pool for redwood-large. Canary traffic ~5%.

anna (sre): Impact matrix? Which customers seeing stalls vs slow tokens?

ryan (oncall): Quick check: p50 unchanged, p95 up, p99 huge. Streaming chunk timeouts spike at chunk index 1-3. Logs show repeated kernel fallback messages and queueing.

leonard (eng-ml): Interesting — calibration changed per-layer quant thresholds; could alter kernel path selection and increase kernel latency for some sequence lengths.

customer-sre: We have two customers reporting streaming interruptions: acme.ai and beta-platform. Tickets 5442, 5447. Both on dedicated pools?

raj (eng-runtime): acme.ai traffic currently on shared-hosted pool, not dedicated. Beta-platform on dedicated, but both received canary-int8 traffic routed by rollout policy.

ryan (oncall): Action plan: 1) divert traffic for redwood-large away from int8-calib profile -> quick API flip. 2) scale up fallback fp16 variant for burst. 3) collect kernel traces + sample requests for analysis. 4) update incident record.

ryan (oncall): Executing step 1 now: calling runtime-control API to update routing.

ryan (oncall): ```
# switch rollouts
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/rollout/switch \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","from":"int8-calib-2026-03-14","to":"fp16-global-fallback","percent":100}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy event: routing-change accepted by control-plane (req_id: rc-8b3f). New route to fp16-global-fallback will take effect in ~30s.

incident-bot: Mitigation: traffic reroute started. Estimated customer impact reduction in 1-2 min.

ryan (oncall): Step 2: scaling up fp16 pool to handle increased qps. Running autoscale override +2x for next 10m.

raj (eng-runtime): Noted. Also temporary throttle streaming chunk size to 512 tokens to reduce KV growth while we stabilize.

anna (sre): I posted targeted alert to SLO dashboard. Marking as SLO breach possible (p99 > 2s). Logging for retrospective.

leonard (eng-ml): Please capture a set of 50 failed streaming requests (headers + model meta + seed prompt). I'll analyze quant kernel hot paths.

ryan (oncall): On it — collecting sample bundle and kernel logs. Command: ``rsync -av /var/logs/runtime/kernels/ recent-bundle:/tmp/incident-1763205123``

customer-sre: Acme.ai reported recovery at ~40s after reroute. Beta-platform still seeing intermittent stalls (dedicated).

raj (eng-runtime): Beta-platform's dedicated pool still had a subset that received int8 due to an old placement rule — fixing placement rule now.

ryan (oncall): Placement rule fix applied. Forcing reconcilers to reassign pods: ``kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/redwood-runtime``

deploy-bot: restart jobs enqueued — expected pod churn ~3m.

maya (oncall-next): Handing on-call to me in 10m. If anything regresses, ping @maya.

anna (sre): Noting impacted customers: acme.ai, beta-platform, one internal test harness. Severity set to P1 for now until p99 < 1s.

ryan (oncall): Collected bundle posted to `/tmp/incident-1763205123/samples.tar.gz`. Leonard, you have access.

leonard (eng-ml): Received. Early look: some attention kernels switched to a fallback slow path when quant scale for layer 9 hits 0.0001 — causes extra memcpy + CPU fallback on certain GPUs. That explains per-request stalls (inconsistent).

leonard (eng-ml): Short-term mitigation idea: adjust calibration thresholds to avoid tiny scales (clamp to min 0.001) and re-deploy. But that's a code change and takes longer than rollback.

ryan (oncall): Agreed — we should prefer rollback of profile for immediate mitigation, then patch calibration to clamp.

raj (eng-runtime): Rollback complete, routing now 100% to fp16-global-fallback and dedicated placement reconciled. Observed p99 back down to ~220ms over last 2m.

incident-bot: Auto updates: p95 170ms, p99 240ms, streaming stall count dropped 93% since routing change.

customer-sre: Followed up with acme.ai and beta-platform — beta-platform reports nominal now. Both ask for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.

anna (sre): I'll draft initial incident note: suspected regression caused by int8 calibration profile producing tiny quant scales -> kernel fallback -> tail stalls. Marking rollback as mitigation.

ryan (oncall): Handoff to maya: I'm going offline in 7m. Maya, keep an eye for any regressions and track RAID (root cause, actions, impact, deadline).

maya (oncall-next): Taking over. I'll coordinate with Leonard for calibration patch and Raj for safe canary plan.

leonard (eng-ml): Plan: 1) create clamp patch + unit tests. 2) run offline perf sim on representative sequences. 3) run staged canary using 1% traffic with extended telemetry. 4) if stable, roll to canary and increment. Target ETA for patch candidate: ~4h.

anna (sre): Postmortem owners: leonard (root cause + fix), raj (deployment/process), ryan/maya (oncall timeline & mitigations). I'll schedule postmortem doc and follow-up.

ryan (oncall): Closing active page — mitigation successful, p99 within SLO. If anything pops within 2h, re-open. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident CLOSED by ryan (oncall) at 1763205789. Summary: rollback of int8-calib profile + routing + placement fix resolved p99 and streaming stalls. Next steps: clamp calibration, controlled canary, postmortem.

maya (oncall-next): Thanks team. I'll start running the staged canary plan later today and update this thread with status.

anna (sre): Adding tickets for customer communications and formal RCA.

leonard (eng-ml): Will include kernel-level trace items in RCA.

ryan (oncall): Great job everyone. :trophy:
